faqs.q: What should I include on a locksmith invoice?
faqs.a: At minimum: your business name and license number, the client and job-site address, a dated line-item list (lockout, picking, rekeying, replacement, keys), tax, and a total due. Most cities require a locksmith license number on the invoice.

faqs.q: Is this template free to use?
faqs.a: Yes. All three formats (PDF, Word, Excel) are free to download with no email required.

faqs.q: Does the Excel version calculate tax automatically?
faqs.a: Yes. Enter your quantity and rate per line, and the subtotal, tax and total update automatically. Leave the tax rate blank if you are not required to charge sales tax.

faqs.q: Do you have a free locksmith invoice I can download?
faqs.a: Yes. This locksmith invoice template is free to download as PDF, Word, or Excel - no email required. It includes pre-filled line items for lockout service, key cutting, rekeying, lock installation, and automotive keys, with fields for your business name and license number.

faqs.q: Is this legal or tax advice?
faqs.a: No. Templates are for informational purposes only. Requirements vary by state and city — verify with your licensing authority and a CPA or attorney before use.

deepDive.heading: Locksmith invoicing: service calls, key cutting and the security work that needs a paper trail
deepDive.sub: Locksmith work splits into three businesses — emergency lockouts, key and cylinder work, and security hardware — and each is priced and documented differently. Here is what belongs on the invoice.

blocks.h3: The lockout call is priced on time of day, not on skill
paras: A residential lockout is a service call: a trip charge plus a rate that depends on the hour. Daytime lockouts typically run $50 to $100 including the trip; evenings, weekends and holidays multiply that by 1.5 to 2.5. Automotive lockouts are higher again because the tools and the risk are different. The invoice should show the base call, the time-of-day multiplier and any hardware separately.

State the price range before dispatch and the final price on the invoice, and never let the multiplier appear for the first time on the bill. Locksmithing has a reputation problem driven by exactly this practice, so an invoice that shows "after-hours rate 1.5x" as a line is both a defence and a marketing asset.
list: Trip/service call charge, stated separately from labour
Time-of-day multiplier shown as its own line
Automotive vs residential vs commercial rates differ — name the category
Damage waiver or lock-destruction charge if drilling was required, approved before drilling

blocks.h3: Key cutting, rekeying and master key systems are priced per unit
paras: Rekeying is priced per cylinder — typically $15 to $35 per lock in a residential setting, more for high-security cylinders or restricted keyways. Cutting keys is priced per key by type: standard, transponder/chip, laser-cut, and restricted. Master key systems carry an additional design and pinning charge because the system has to be planned before any cylinder is pinned.

The invoice should list cylinder count and location (front door, back door, garage entry), key type and quantity, and whether the customer received a control card for restricted keys. That control card matters: without it, the customer cannot order more keys later, and the invoice is the record that proves they were given one.
list: Cylinders rekeyed: count and location, price each
Keys cut: quantity and type (standard, transponder, laser, restricted)
Master key system: design/pinning charge plus per-cylinder cost
Restricted key control card issued — note it on the invoice
Hardware supplied vs customer-supplied, with warranty consequences

blocks.h3: Security hardware and the installation record
paras: Deadbolts, electronic locks, panic hardware and access control are installation work with a warranty, and the invoice is the installation record. Grade matters: ANSI/BHMA Grade 1 hardware is specified on commercial doors and costs several times a Grade 3 residential deadbolt. When a customer later claims the lock failed, the grade on the invoice is what determines whether the hardware was appropriate for the door.

Access control and electronic locks also need the commissioning details: who holds the master code, how many user codes were programmed, whether the audit trail was enabled. Leaving without transferring that information is how a locksmith ends up being called back to a site for free.
list: Hardware make, model and ANSI/BHMA grade
Door type and preparation required (new bore, wrap plate, strike reinforcement)
Electronic locks: user codes programmed, master code transferred, audit trail status
Warranty: hardware manufacturer warranty vs your installation warranty

blocks.h3: Commercial and property-management work needs a signed work order
paras: Commercial locksmith work usually runs through a property manager or a facilities contract, and the invoicing convention is a work order number per site visit with the authorising person named. Without that, a $600 master key job on a 40-unit building becomes a collections problem.

The other commercial convention is the keying schedule: which key opens which doors, how many copies exist, and who holds them. That schedule is a security document. It should be delivered to the client, acknowledged in writing, and the invoice should say it was issued — because if a key goes missing, the first question will be who had a copy.
list: Work order number and authorising contact on every invoice
Keying schedule issued and acknowledged
Number of keys cut and to whom released
Response-time obligations if the contract has an SLA
Site access notes: escort required, badge, after-hours procedure

blocks.h3: Paper tickets still matter for mobile locksmiths
paras: A mobile locksmith works out of a van with no office nearby. A two-part carbonless ticket printed from this template — white for the customer, yellow for the van file — is the practical record, and the customer signature is what makes a chargeback survivable.

The fields a locksmith ticket needs beyond a generic invoice: vehicle year/make/model for automotive work, VIN where a key is being cut by code, proof of ownership check for automotive lockouts (registration or title sighted), and the cylinder or lock identified by location on the property. Automotive work in particular is a fraud-sensitive area, and documenting that you verified ownership protects you as much as the customer.
list: Automotive: year, make, model, VIN, ownership document sighted
Property: which door/cylinder, described by location
Method used: bypass, pick, drill — with customer approval for destructive entry
Keys issued: quantity and type, signed for by the customer
Customer signature and date on both copies
